notes: `לְיַד` → *was to wait on* is one fused rendering of which no morpheme owns a part, headed on the construct noun with the lexical anchor *wait* (rules 23, 24, 30), the copula joining it under rules 20 and 49. The competing reading splits *to* onto the preposition.

In `מַעֲשֵׂה עֲבֹדַת בֵּית הָאֱלֹהִים` three *the*s answer to one article morpheme: the article's stands before *house*, the word its own noun immediately depends on, and the two outer constructs take supplied ones (rule 29).
The *of* before *all holy things* answers to the written `לְ`, not to a construct relation (rule 19).
The marginal gloss *Hebrew their station was at the hand of the sons of Aaron* corroborates the fused reading of `לְיַד` and decides nothing (rules 7, 38).
